name: fmt_journey_map
caption:
HOW RJ GOT HOME 🗺️🦖 Born in Toronto. About 15,000 miles later, he's ours.

🍁 Mississauga: St. Marcellinus, 27 points in a game as a freshman. Godfather: Steve Nash
🌴 Montverde, FL (2015): 22 PPG and 7 RPG as a sophomore
🇪🇬 Cairo (2017): 38 and 13 on the USA in the U19 World Cup semis. Gold + MVP
🌴 Back in Florida: national champs, every major player of the year award
😈 Duke: 22.6 PPG next to Zion, first-team All-American
🗽 New York: No. 3 pick in 2019, youngest Knick ever to average 20
🦖 Dec 30, 2023: traded home. 19 and 9 in his first game, a win
📈 This season: 21.3 PPG through 10 games

Miles are great-circle distances between stops, rounded. Where should his road go next? 👇

beats.vo: From Mississauga to Toronto, RJ Barrett traveled about fifteen thousand miles to get home.
Let's run it back.

beats.head: MISSISSAUGA, ON
beats.vo: Mississauga, Ontario.

beats.head: MISSISSAUGA, ON
beats.vo: As a freshman at St. Marcellinus, he dropped twenty-seven in a game.
beats.dlg: FRESHMAN YEAR:|27 POINTS IN ONE GAME!

beats.head: MISSISSAUGA, ON
beats.vo: And he trained with his godfather, Steve Nash.

beats.head: NEXT STOP: FLORIDA
beats.vo: At fifteen, he left home for Montverde Academy in Florida.
beats.dlg: AT 15, HE LEFT HOME|FOR MONTVERDE, FLORIDA.

beats.head: MONTVERDE, FL
beats.vo: As a sophomore: twenty-two points and seven rebounds a game.

beats.head: NEXT STOP: EGYPT
beats.vo: Summer twenty seventeen: Cairo, for the Under-19 World Cup.

beats.head: CAIRO, EGYPT
beats.vo: Semifinal against the USA: thirty-eight points and thirteen rebounds.
beats.dlg: SEMIS VS THE USA:|38 POINTS, 13 BOARDS!

beats.head: CAIRO, EGYPT
beats.vo: Canada won gold. He was the tournament MVP.

beats.head: BACK TO FLORIDA
beats.vo: Back in Florida, senior year: a national title, and every major player of the year award.

beats.head: NEXT STOP: DUKE
beats.vo: Then Duke.

beats.head: DURHAM, NC
beats.vo: Twenty-two point six points a night, next to Zion Williamson. First-team All-American.
beats.dlg: 22.6 A NIGHT NEXT TO ZION.|FIRST-TEAM ALL-AMERICAN!

beats.head: NEXT STOP: NEW YORK
beats.vo: Draft night, twenty nineteen.

beats.head: NEW YORK, NY
beats.vo: The Knicks took him third.

beats.head: NEW YORK, NY
beats.vo: At twenty-one, the youngest Knick ever to average twenty a game.
beats.dlg: THE YOUNGEST KNICK EVER|TO AVERAGE 20 A GAME.

beats.head: THE TRADE
beats.vo: Then, December thirtieth, twenty twenty-three, we traded for him.

beats.head: TORONTO, ON
beats.vo: His first game home: nineteen points and nine rebounds in a win.
beats.dlg: FIRST GAME HOME:|19 POINTS, 9 BOARDS, A WIN!

beats.head: TORONTO, ON
beats.vo: And this season: twenty-one point three a night through ten games.

beats.head: WELCOME HOME
beats.vo: Born in Toronto. About fifteen thousand miles later, he's home.
beats.dlg: BORN IN TORONTO... 15,000|MILES LATER, HE'S HOME.

facts.claim: RJ Barrett, born June 14, 2000 in Toronto; family settled in Mississauga in 2008; began high school at St. Marcellinus in Mississauga (2014-15), 27-point effort as a freshman on October 9, 2014; trained with Steve Nash, his godfather; in September 2015 transferred to Montverde Academy (2015-18); sophomore season 2016-17: 22 points and 7 rebounds per game, National Sophomore of the Year; July 2017 FIBA U19 World Cup: 38 points, 13 rebounds, 5 assists in a 99-87 semifinal win over the US; Canada won gold, Barrett MVP; senior year (2017-18): first player since LeBron James to sweep all major awards and win the national championship; Duke 2018-19: 22.6 points, 7.6 rebounds, 4.3 assists, consensus first-team (1ST-TEAM) All-American, teammate Zion Williamson; June 20, 2019 Knicks drafted him third overall (No. 3, 3RD) in the 2019 NBA draft; youngest Knicks player to average 20 points per game, at 21; December 30, 2023 traded with Quickley to Toronto for Anunoby, Achiuwa and Flynn; January 1, 2024 (JAN 2024): 19 points, 9 rebounds in a 124-121 win over Cleveland

Level = age at each stop (born June 14, 2000): LV 14 in 2014-15, LV 16 in 2016-17, LV 17 in July 2017, LV 18 in 2018-19, LV 19 in June 2019, LV 21 in 2021-22, LV 23 in Jan 2024, LV 26 in 2026-27; at 15 he left for Montverde (Sept 2015); map tags by year: Mississauga 2014, Montverde 2015, Cairo 2017, back to Montverde 2017, Durham 2018, New York 2019, Toronto 2023
The 2017 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup was held in Cairo, Egypt from 1 to 9 July 2017; Canada won gold, MVP R. J. Barrett (U19)
